## `Restart-when:` written — ⛔ hold KEPT. ⚠️⚠️ **And the card's own wake condition HAS ALREADY FIRED: 0.49x → 0.32x.**

PM seat `domain:devx @ objectui`, session `session_01FhBNJcLRZLe8M87VcUgpKr`, 2026-09-13T14:40Z. objectui#8587 conversion sweep.

### Why this card was the sharpest floor case in this lane

Measured across all 10 of this lane's holds: objectui#6319 was one of **three** carrying **no hold predicate in its body or its comments**, and the only one with **zero discussion comments at all**. ⇒ ⛔ a hold with no predicate and no thread is indistinguishable from a card someone forgot — which is precisely what objectui#8587 exists to end.

### ⭐ The predicate was in the card's own prose all along

> its size is set by the aggregate headroom — **44.0 KB against an 89.0 KB regression class (0.49x)** at the time of writing. **If a future re-baseline tightens that further, the residual gets proportionally more room to hide in, and whoever tightens it should see this card rather than rediscover it.**

⇒ machine-readable:

```
Restart-when: the eager-closure AGGREGATE headroom ratio printed by
              scripts/check-eager-closure-budget.mjs falls below the 0.49x
              recorded at filing — i.e. the `Bundle Analysis` job's line
                "aggregate closure … (headroom N KB = R x the 89.0 KB regression)"
              reports R < 0.49.
              Read it from any recent Bundle Analysis run's log; no local build needed.
```

### ⚠️⚠️ It has fired — measured today, incidentally, on someone else's PR

`Bundle Analysis` on PR objectui#9388, **2026-09-13T10:30Z**, printed verbatim:

```
✅ Console eager closure is 3105.9 KB gzipped across 52 of 528 chunks
   (budget: 3134.8 KB, headroom: 28.9 KB).
✅ aggregate closure  3105.9 KB measured / 3134.8 KB ceiling
   (headroom 28.9 KB = 0.32x the 89.0 KB regression)
```

| | at filing, 2026-08-25 | today, 2026-09-13 |
|:--|--:|--:|
| aggregate headroom | **44.0 KB** | **28.9 KB** |
| as a fraction of the 89.0 KB regression class | **0.49x** | **0.32x** |

⇒ **−15.1 KB, 0.49x → 0.32x, in 19 days.** ⛔ The ratio is **the gate's own printed figure**, ⛔ not my arithmetic.

⇒ ⭐⭐ **The card predicted exactly this and predicted that nobody would see it**: 「whoever tightens it should see this card rather than rediscover it」. The headroom tightened, and this card was seen only because an unrelated sweep read it. ⚠️ It was also **not** seen by me this morning, when I read that very `Bundle Analysis` log in detail while establishing an inherited red on objectui#9388 — I had the number in front of me and did not connect it to a held card.

### ⛔ Why the hold STAYS despite the trigger

The card is explicitly 「**recorded rather than fixed**」. Its only in-repo remedy is objectui#6245's body option 1 — *require branches to be up to date before merging* — which is a **repository setting, ⛔ not code**, changing every seat's queue in a repo doing ~18 merges/day. The card itself puts that 「squarely on the maintainer floor」 and ⛔ **neither the filing seat nor the implementing dev proposed it**.

⇒ ⛔ Firing the predicate does **not** make this dispatchable. It makes it **visible**, which is what it was filed for. `pm:on-hold` is kept, now **with** a predicate, and the trigger is recorded above where the next reader meets it.

⚠️ ⭐ **For whoever re-baselines next**: this is the card the prose told you to find. The residual is a verdict that FINISHES before a ceiling moves, on a PR merged after — ⛔ no code of ours runs at that moment, and GitHub does not re-run a PR's checks when the base moves. The `push`-on-`main` run detects it **after the fact** — ⭐ **a detection, ⛔ not a gate** — and the size of the window it hides in is the headroom above, which has now shrunk by a third.

⛔ No script, gate or label added. ⛔ `domain:devx` unchanged; ⛔ no `priority:*` produced — this card carries none and this seat does not grade.

## ⚠️⚠️ This hold's stated reason may be DISCHARGED — the repository setting it names reads **`true`** today. ⛔ Hold KEPT; ⛔ I am not unlocking on an unmeasured inference.

`domain:devx @ objectui` seat, `session_013VGeMu3p6qEFWR6K6GGLaW`, R58, 2026-09-14T13:4xZ, unlock scan over this lane's 27 held cards.

### What the hold rests on

`5653925497` kept this hold with this reasoning, quoted:

> Its only in-repo remedy is objectui#6245's body option 1 — *require branches to be up to date before merging* — which is a **repository setting, ⛔ not code** … ⛔ **neither the filing seat nor the implementing dev proposed it**.

objectui#6245's option 1, verbatim:

> 1. **Require the branch to be up to date before merging** (repo setting) — closes it for every required context at once, at the cost of more re-runs on a repo doing ~18 merges/day.

### ⭐ The measurement

`GET /repos/objectstack-ai/objectui/rules/branches/main`, read today while working objectui#9499:

```
required_status_checks:
  Lint · Type Check · Build & E2E · Test (shard 1/4 … 4/4) · Build Docs · Changeset Declaration
  strict_required_status_checks_policy: true      ⬅
merge_queue:
  check_response_timeout_minutes: 60
```

**CONTROL, same endpoint, one argument changed**: `rules/branches/zzz-no-such-branch-9499` returns **`200 []`** ⇒ the reader distinguishes *"a branch with rules"* from *"a branch with none"*, so the `true` is a reading and ⛔ not a default.

⇒ **`strict_required_status_checks_policy` IS "require branches to be up to date before merging".** The setting this hold says nobody applied reads **on**.

### ⛔ Why I am NOT unlocking

⛔ **I have not established that this resolves the card**, and the obvious reading is exactly the kind this lane keeps filing errata about:

1. ⛔ **The merge-queue interaction is UNMEASURED.** This repo runs a merge queue, which builds and tests its own merge commit; how `strict_required_status_checks_policy` composes with that — whether it is enforced, superseded, or simply redundant — is ⛔ not something I measured, and I will not assert it.
2. ⛔ **When the setting was turned on is unknown to me.** The ruleset's `updated_at` is **2026-08-24**; this card was filed **2026-08-25**. ⚠️ Those are one day apart in the *wrong* direction for a tidy story, and ⛔ a ruleset `updated_at` does not tell you *which field* changed.
3. ⭐ The card's residual is specifically the window where a verdict **finishes**, then a ceiling **moves**, then the PR merges. Whether an up-to-date requirement closes *that* window — as opposed to the simpler stale-checkout case objectui#6245 described — needs a measurement, ⛔ not an inference from the flag's name.

⇒ **`pm:on-hold` KEPT.** What changes is that the hold's stated reason is now **in question** rather than settled, and that is recorded where the next reader meets it.

### What would settle it — one measurement, named

Establish whether a PR whose `Bundle Analysis` finished **before** a ceiling change can still reach `main` today. ⭐ The instrument already exists and is free: the same `push`-on-`main` detection the card calls *"a detection, ⛔ not a gate"*. If it has stopped firing since the setting went on, that is evidence; if it still fires, the residual is live and the hold was right.

⚠️ ⛔ Do not answer this by reading the flag's name. **Answer it with a run.**

### ⭐ And this is the SECOND card in this lane resting on "that surface is unreadable"

**objectui#9502**, filed today: two places in the tree tell authors the required-check surface is *"a repository-settings surface nothing here can read"* and that the shard jobs are not required — **both false today**, both true when written.

⇒ this card is the same shape from the other side: a hold whose premise is *"only a repo setting could fix it, and nobody can see or change it."* ⭐ The surface **is** readable, by an ordinary token, through a documented endpoint — and two cards in this lane have been reasoning without it. ⇒ objectui#9502's repair (point at the endpoint instead of restating its answer) would have surfaced this 20 days ago.

⚠️ The prior seat's own note on this card is worth keeping beside that: it had the decisive number **in front of it** in a `Bundle Analysis` log that morning and did not connect it to a held card. ⇒ the failure is not carelessness, it is that **nothing routes a reading to the card that is waiting for it**.

⛔ No label changed beyond none; ⛔ no `priority:*` produced (this card carries none and this seat does not grade it); ⛔ `domain:devx` unchanged.
